clue.text: Teams drink a cold tea — more than one sugar needed

definitions.note: plural phrase for a plural noun

indicators.note: the teams swallow what follows, so it ends up inside them

parts.note: teams are sides in a match
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
char is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Players at a break sip a cold cup of tea and want it sweeter.
explanation.walkthrough: Char is British slang for tea; the cold tea goes down the teams' throats, so it ends up inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharides are the chemical class of sugars, so the plural names several sugar molecules.

clue.text: Vessel's taking a bit over a lake

definitions.note: the possessive works as an adjective, of the vessel

parts.note: taken as written
an ort is a scrap or leftover morsel
taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A boat carries a small load across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' just places the first pair above the second. The vessel is a blood vessel, the aorta, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Aortal is the adjective for the aorta, the main artery, which is a blood vessel.

clue.text: Tissues pocketed by hypochondriacs

indicators.note: something pocketed sits inside another, so the letters are tucked within the following word

parts.note: the run of letters sitting in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: Worried patients stuff their pockets with paper hankies.
explanation.definitionFit: Chondri is a plural of chondrus, cartilage, which is a body tissue; the surface pretends they are paper hankies.

clue.text: Pole outside pub in estate surrounded by a watery expanse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what is surrounded sits within the thing around it, here the expanse of water

parts.note: a lake is a broad body of water
EST is an abbreviation for estate

explanation.surface: A pub sign on a housing estate stands beside a reservoir.
explanation.walkthrough: The estate is enclosed after the first letter of the expanse of water, not at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An ale-stake was the pole set up outside an alehouse as its sign, hung with a garland or bush.

clue.text: One boy absorbing island story of adventure

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the boy soaks up what follows, holding it inside himself

parts.note: a lad is a boy
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A lone boy is engrossed in a tale of island adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside LAD, after the opening I.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War is a long heroic tale, and the word also means any long series of adventures.

clue.text: Peer's domain wanting tax — customs house is installed for short time

indicators.note: one thing installed for another takes its place, swapping one item out

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods
CH is the abbreviation for custom house
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A nobleman's estate is short of funds, and a customs post goes up for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: CH takes the place of the T in DUTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchy is the territory ruled by a duke, and a duke is a peer of the realm.

clue.text: Separate, using form of screen

indicators.note: a different form of the word means its letters are recast into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Keeping things apart by putting up some kind of partition.
explanation.definitionFit: To secern is an old verb meaning to discriminate or set apart, a synonym for the verb separate.

clue.text: Boorish old fools in activity on the block?

indicators.note: places the jumbled letters inside the activity named next

parts.note: chopping is done on a chopping block, the question mark flagging the stretch

indicators.note: used as a verb, to fool something is to mess it about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Uncouth old idiots busy at the executioner's block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old fools' reads as a noun phrase; 'fools' is a verb acting on 'old', and the jumble lands after the first letter of the block activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Clodhopping describes someone clumsy and loutish, like a heavy-booted yokel, so it fits uncouth behaviour.

clue.text: Christmas involves companion giving financial warning

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the companion is enclosed by the festive word

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
CH is Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A Christmas visitor arrives with a warning about the household budget.
explanation.walkthrough: Companion of Honour is a British order whose initials crosswords use for companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Nochel is an old Scots verb meaning to refuse to honour a debt or to give notice of non-payment, a money warning.

clue.text: Wine served by inn with retirees getting drunk

indicators.note: drunken people lurch about, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub serves white wine to pensioners who get tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nierstein is a Rhine town whose white wine, a hock, is sold under this name.

clue.text: Piano rendering what could be gleeful lacking heart

indicators.note: a rendering is a fresh version, so the remaining letters are re-rendered in another order
the word loses its central letter, as if its heart were cut out

parts.note: taken as written, before the middle letter goes

explanation.surface: A pianist's performance that ought to be joyful has no soul.
explanation.walkthrough: GLEEFUL has seven letters, so its fourth, an E, is the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Flügel is German for a grand piano, the wing-shaped instrument, and English dictionaries list it for that keyboard.

clue.text: Arguing Europeans interrupted by Monsieur in charge

definitions.note: a verbal noun standing for the plural noun

indicators.note: something interrupted is broken into, so another element sits in its middle

parts.note: people from Poland are Europeans
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur
IC is short for in charge

explanation.surface: Continental visitors bickering are broken up by a Frenchman taking command.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a gerund standing in for the noun: arguing as an activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemics is the practice of controversy and disputation, the art of arguing a case.

clue.text: Old plants thespian's written about

indicators.note: written about suggests letters set down in a scattered, roundabout way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor writes a piece about old garden flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the fodder to its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Penthia is an obsolete name for a plant, said to be a kind of flowering herb, so the plural is old plants.

clue.text: Not all having to collect money turned up — four such would get round together?

definitions.text: four such would get round together?

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so one element holds the other

parts.note: some means not all

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from the bottom to the top

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: Only part of the cash arrived, and a few people had to go round collecting it.
explanation.walkthrough: A dime is a US ten-cent coin. The definition is cryptic: quarter-domes put together, it suggests, make a full round dome.
explanation.definitionFit: A semidome is a half-dome roofing an apse; the clue playfully imagines joining such pieces into one rounded vault.

clue.text: Big fellows — a number seen in French art

indicators.note: something seen in another is found within it, so one element sits inside

parts.note: es is French for 'art', as in thou art
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Giants appear among the numbers in a French gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the verb form, thou art, which in French is tu es; it is not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Eten is an old word for a giant, so the plural names big men.

clue.text: A male locked in primitive building becomes a martyr

indicators.note: something locked in is shut inside, here inside the building

parts.note: a shed is a basic, rough building
taken as written
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man shut away in a crude hut ends up a martyr.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becomes' is only the link; the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaheed is an Arabic-derived word for a Muslim martyr, one who dies for the faith.

clue.text: Some beer and you will get aroused!

indicators.note: only part of the following words is taken, a stretch running across them

parts.note: a run of letters crossing these three words

explanation.surface: A few drinks and you'll feel amorous.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is informal British for sexually excited, a synonym for aroused.

clue.text: President in top position for arguing a cause

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for president
leading means being in first place

explanation.surface: A president at the head of affairs champions a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleading is the advocate's work in court, putting a case for one side.

clue.text: Friend has a sort of coat for horse

parts.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written
a mino is a Japanese straw raincoat

explanation.surface: A friend owns a particular coat colour suited to a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a horse's coat colour, which is how a palomino is known, but the coat here is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Palamino is a variant spelling of palomino, a golden horse with a pale mane and tail.

clue.text: Rodent eats insect and tropical plants

indicators.note: whatever is eaten ends up inside the eater

parts.note: the mara is a long-legged South American rodent, the Patagonian cavy
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A rodent snacks on a bug among the jungle greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Maranta is a genus of tropical American herbs, including arrowroot and the prayer plant.

clue.text: Young female nabbed by fellow made a noise with tongue

indicators.note: something nabbed is grabbed and held, so it ends up inside its captor

parts.note: Ted is a man's name, a fellow
chick is slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: A girl is caught by a chap and clicks her tongue in disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: To tchick is to make a clicking sound with the tongue, as of annoyance or to urge on a horse.

clue.text: Coins celebrate independence

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully in celebration
I is the abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: Commemorative coins are struck to mark a nation's freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Caroli is the plural of carolus, an old gold coin of King Charles's reign.

clue.text: Highest place heated? The lowest actually!

parts.note: the top is the highest place
het is a dialect past participle of heat

explanation.surface: A place at the summit gets hot, though it is really the depths.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves build 'highest place heated', yet the whole is the lowest place of all: hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Tophet is a biblical name for hell, the hottest and lowest of places in the underworld.

clue.text: Group in company set up before new year

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting up raises the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival

explanation.surface: A band within a firm is formed just ahead of New Year.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a set of eight, especially eight musicians playing together.

clue.text: Vet maybe about to penetrate dog

indicators.note: something that penetrates goes into another thing, here into the dog

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An animal doctor is about to give a dog an injection.
explanation.definitionFit: A vet heals sick animals, so is one example of someone who cures; 'maybe' flags the example.

clue.text: Soldiers knocked back drink? Nothing to be admitted

indicators.note: knocked back here means sent backwards, so the letters run the other way
something admitted is let inside, so this letter goes within the drink

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The squaddies downed their drinks, but none would own up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking; here it is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a body of soldiers, and the plural troops simply means soldiers.

clue.text: Cad afflicted with ruin inclined to fly off the handle

definitions.text: inclined to fly off the handle

indicators.note: something afflicted is damaged and disordered, so the letters are thrown out of shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bounder facing ruin is quick to lose his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Iracund means prone to anger, from Latin ira, rage, so it describes someone with a short temper.

clue.text: Porridge one gives character in Greece?

parts.note: samp is a coarse maize porridge
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bowl of porridge reveals the nature of a Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'character' is a letter of an alphabet, not a person's nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampi is an archaic letter of the Greek alphabet, used for the numeral 900.

clue.text: Steering carelessly, lost grip?

indicators.note: something done carelessly ends up disordered, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A careless driver loses control of the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' marks an obsolete word: Spenser's streigne means to constrain or clasp tightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Streigne is a Spenserian form of strain, meaning to hold tightly, an archaic word for a firm grip.

clue.text: Records set by South African sportsman crossing water

indicators.note: the sportsman spans the water, so it lies within his name

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer
pee is slang for urine, water

explanation.surface: A South African athlete sets records as he crosses a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Elpees spells out LPs, long-playing vinyl records.

clue.text: Kitchen item in stone cask knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the letters run back to front

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
a tun is a large barrel

explanation.surface: A kitchen item stored in a stone barrel gets tipped over.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is a spice kept in the kitchen cupboard, so it is one example of a kitchen item.

clue.text: International ceremony interrupted by flighty type, female plotter

parts.note: INT is the abbreviation for international

indicators.note: something interrupted is broken into, so another element lands in its middle

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
a guan is a South American game bird

explanation.surface: A grand global ceremony is disrupted by a scatterbrained woman with a secret plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' suggests a fickle person; here it is a bird that flies, the guan, a turkey-like bird of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Intriguante is the French-derived feminine form of intriguant, a woman who schemes and plots.
